assertions.name: only_the_massless_channel_is_super_extensive
assertions.note: a Yukawa weight exp(-mu r) with mu > 0 makes the pair sum extensive; mu = 0 weights all n(n-1)/2 pairs by 1. Lean: massless_pair_sum, no_linear_bound_on_pairs

assertions.name: all_three_rates_are_strictly_positive
assertions.note: b < 1 for every letter, so mu = -ln b > 0 always. There is no q at which the framework produces a massless channel

assertions.name: the_pp_and_nn_rates_sum_to_two_log_two_q
assertions.note: from b_pp.b_nn = 1/[2]_q^2. Lean: rate_sum_pinned. So three rates carry ONE constraint and one free parameter q -- any proposal moving one rate moves another

assertions.name: the_range_ratios_are_derived_and_scale_free
assertions.note: lambda_pp/lambda_nn = 1.8519359, fixed by q alone with no length scale. The p-p channel is the longest-ranged, n-n the shortest -- which is the same ordering as the bond strengths

assertions.name: the_letters_fail_the_tree_threshold_above_coordination_three
assertions.note: NONE of the three rates clears ln(d-1) for d >= 4. This is the TREE worst case and it does NOT bind a nucleus: a packing in R^3 has polynomial shell growth ~k^2, for which every mu > 0 converges. Recorded because it is easy to reach for and would be a false alarm

assertions.name: the_framework_s_own_decay_reaches_far_past_first_contact
assertions.note: p-p reaches 173.2256979 effective sites against 12 contacts (14.435475x), so a range-1 truncation discards ~93 % of the weight the same framework's decay rate supplies. Summing b^d(i,j) over all pairs needs NO new parameter -- it is the derived letters at their own range

assertions.name: but_the_growth_class_is_unchanged
assertions.note: every per-site sum is FINITE, so full-range is still O(n). The constant moves 14x, the growth class does not. Section 4 is an option for the STRONG channel and cannot touch EM

parameters.mediator_masses_provenance: PDG, EXTERNAL reference constants used only to place the channels on the range axis
